title: Best NFL APIs in 2026: 8 options for scores, stats, and injuries
summary: The best NFL APIs in 2026 compared: Firecrawl Alexandria, Sportradar, SportsDataIO, API-Sports, BALLDONTLIE, and more, with free tiers, prices, and endpoints.
body_markdown:

API Best for Free option

Prices and free tiers below were checked on November 19, 2026, against each provider's own pages, and they can change.


---


Most NFL side projects stall on data in the first week. You want this week's injury report, last Sunday's box scores, or the standings after week 11, and the NFL does not hand out API keys. So you pick between a licensed feed priced for sportsbooks, a cheap API with a daily quota, or a data dump from the open-source community.


Which one fits depends on the job. A betting model needs play-by-play and odds. A Discord bot needs scores and a free tier. An AI agent answering "is the starting quarterback playing Sunday?" needs the weekly practice report as clean JSON, without five vendor contracts.


This post compares eight options across agent tools, commercial feeds, budget APIs, and open data. If you're building an NFL analytics app, these are the best NFL APIs that you should consider, with a breakdown of price and limits. If your project is about fantasy projections rather than league data, read[the best fantasy data tools for AI agents](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/best-fantasy-data-tools-ai-agents) instead, which ranks those tools on FantasyBench.


## What is an NFL API?


An NFL API is a web service that returns National Football League data, such as schedules, live scores, box scores, player stats, rosters, standings, and injury reports, as structured JSON or XML. Developers call it from apps, dashboards, betting models, and AI agents instead of copying numbers off sports sites by hand.


NFL APIs fall into four groups:


- **Agent data libraries** such as Firecrawl Alexandria, which put several NFL sources behind one key and return JSON an agent can read directly.
- **Licensed real-time feeds** such as Sportradar, built for sportsbooks, broadcasters, and media companies.
- **Developer APIs with tiers** such as API-Sports, BALLDONTLIE, and Highlightly, priced by request quota.
- **Open data** such as nflverse, published as files and packages rather than a hosted endpoint.


## How should you choose an NFL API?


Choose an NFL API by the freshest data you need, the history you need, and who reads the response. Live in-game play-by-play needs a real-time feed like Sportradar or SportsDataIO. Weekly injuries, schedules, and standings work from cheaper APIs or Firecrawl Alexandria. Season-long modeling works from nflverse's free history.


Four questions narrow the list fast:


1. **How fresh?** Live game state, weekly reports, or past seasons only.
2. **How much history?** The current season, two seasons, or two decades.
3. **Who reads it?** Your own code, or an AI agent that has to pick the right call.
4. **What can you spend?** A free tier, a hobby plan, or a sales quote.


## The best NFL APIs in 2026


## 1. Firecrawl Alexandria


**[Firecrawl Alexandria](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/) is Firecrawl's library of data providers, and its sports data providers include NFL.com and ESPN, both returning JSON through one Firecrawl API key.**


Firecrawl Alexandria lists 550+ providers that an agent can search for free and call by name. For the NFL, two matter most. The[NFL.com provider](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/nfl-com) reads nfl.com's own API for weekly injury and practice reports, rosters, standings, schedules with scores, games, player profiles, and news. The[ESPN provider](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/espn-com) adds scoreboards, box scores with passing, rushing, and receiving lines, team schedules, rosters, player career stats, and league injury lists.


I ran the NFL.com injury report for the Kansas City Chiefs on November 19, 2026. It returned 15 players, each with practice status by day (FULL, LIMITED, or DIDNOT), the practice injury, and the game designation, for 5 Firecrawl credits.


- ` sports-league-data/injury_report` : The weekly NFL.com practice and injury report, league-wide or for one club
- ` sports-league-data/schedule` : Games for a week with scores, broadcast networks, and game IDs
- ` sports-league-data/standings` and` team_roster` : Division standings, records, and club rosters
- ` sports-data/scoreboard` and` boxscore` (ESPN): Live and final scores, then player stat lines per game
- **Fantasy sources on the same key** : Projections and rankings from CBS Sports, Draft Sharks, StartWho, FFToday, and more
- **Works in AI apps** : Ask in ChatGPT or Claude through the Firecrawl plugin and connector, or call it from Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor


### How did NFL.com and ESPN score on the Firecrawl Alexandria benchmark?


Firecrawl Alexandria publishes a[sports stats and results benchmark](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/benchmarks/sports-stats) built from real agent calls over the last 24 hours. Quality is the share of calls answered without a tool error, and speed is P95 latency. Here's how the NFL providers scored at the time of publication:


Provider Quality Speed (P95) Cost per call Calls (24 hours)


ESPN **99.5%** **752 ms** 5 Firecrawl credits 1,000+


NFL.com **96.5%** 4.1 s 5 Firecrawl credits 289


The NFL.com injury report tool scored 100% quality on 206 calls in the same window. These numbers move daily, so check the[benchmarks page](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/benchmarks) for the current read.


**Install:**


```text
# CLI and skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other agents
npx   -y   firecrawl-cli@latest   init   --all   --browser


# Python SDK
pip   install   firecrawl-py
```


**Example:**


```text
import   os
from   firecrawl   import   Firecrawl


firecrawl   =   Firecrawl  (api_key  =  os.environ.  get  (  "FIRECRAWL_API_KEY"  ))


doc   =   firecrawl  .  scrape  (
alexandria  =  {
"provider"  :   "nfl-com"  ,
"capability"  :   "sports-league-data/injury_report"  ,
"options"  : {  "team"  :   "KC"  },
},
)


result   =   doc  .  alexandria  [  0  ]
if   result  .  error  :
raise   RuntimeError  (  f  "nfl-com/injury_report:   {  result.error  }  "  )


for   row   in   result  .  data  [  "reports"  ]:
print  (row[  "player"  ][  "display_name"  ], row[  "practice_status"  ], row[  "injury_status"  ])
```


Or ask in plain English from ChatGPT or Claude:


```text
Use Firecrawl Alexandria to show the Chiefs' injury report
from NFL.com for this week.
```


[Add Firecrawl to ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a314a73f8ac819195b0d55e36b9c609?q=firecrawl)[Add Firecrawl to Claude](https://claude.ai/directory/connectors/firecrawl)


[Apex](https://x.com/apex_ether) , a founder, shared the result on X:


**Honest take:** For agents, this is the shortest path from a question to the weekly practice report, and ESPN fills in scores and box scores on the same key. In-game betting needs second-by-second play-by-play, so pair it with a licensed feed for that job.


**Cons:** Needs a Firecrawl account, signed in through the plugin, connector, or MCP, or a Firecrawl API key, since Alexandria doesn't run keyless. Each call costs Firecrawl credits, and the free plan's 1,000 monthly Firecrawl credits cover testing rather than a production bot. See[Firecrawl pricing](https://www.firecrawl.dev/pricing) for plans and how many Firecrawl credits each one includes.


Full reference at the[sports category page](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/categories/sports) and the[sports data docs](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/use-cases/sports-fantasy) .


## 2. Sportradar


**[Sportradar's NFL API](https://developer.sportradar.com/football/reference/nfl-overview) is a licensed real-time feed with full play-by-play for every game, including preseason.**


Sportradar's NFL docs describe primary feeds for schedules, standings, team and player data, and real-time scores (compiled by its in-house operators). Additional feeds cover team rosters, depth charts, weekly injuries, seasonal statistics, subjective statistics, and draft information.


- **Play-by-play** : Full coverage for every NFL game, preseason included
- **Depth charts and injuries** : Weekly injury feeds and depth charts as separate endpoints
- **Push feeds** : Four delivery feeds for real-time customers
- **Formats** : JSON or XML, authenticated with an` x-api-key` header


**Example:**


```text
curl   "https://api.sportradar.com/nfl/official/trial/v7/en/league/hierarchy.json"   \
-H   "x-api-key: YOUR_SPORTRADAR_API_KEY"
```


**Honest take:** Sportradar is the depth option, and its docs say the APIs are intended for B2B use. That framing fits sportsbooks and media companies better than weekend projects.


**Cons:** The NFL docs pages don't list prices. You start with a trial key from the[Sportradar marketplace](https://marketplace.sportradar.com/signup) and contact the company about production access.


Reference:[Sportradar NFL API basics](https://developer.sportradar.com/football/docs/nfl-ig-api-basics) .


## 3. SportsDataIO


**[SportsDataIO](https://sportsdata.io/nfl-api) is an NFL data API that bundles scores, stats, odds, fantasy projections, news, and images in one feed.**


SportsDataIO's NFL page splits coverage into pregame, live, and postgame. Pregame covers schedules, rosters, depth charts, injuries, weather forecasts, referee crews, odds, and weekly fantasy projections. Live covers scores, game state, team and player stats, play-by-play, and in-play odds. Postgame adds split stats, snap counts, and red zone and third down stats.


- **Odds and props** : Game lines, player props, futures, and line movement
- **Fantasy data** : Weekly and season-long projections, DFS salaries, ADP, and auction values
- **History** : A historical database for past seasons, scoped with its team
- **Formats** : XML and JSON


**Honest take:** SportsDataIO covers more NFL data types in one feed than any other API in this list, which suits betting and fantasy products. You map the features you need to its available feeds before you start.


**Cons:** The NFL API page offers a[free trial](https://sportsdata.io/free-trial) and a contact form rather than a public price list.


Reference:[SportsDataIO NFL API documentation](https://sportsdata.io/developers/api-documentation/nfl) .


## 4. API-Sports


**[API-Sports](https://api-sports.io/sports/nfl) is a REST API for NFL and NCAA football with a free tier and paid plans sized by daily requests.**


API-Sports covers schedules, historical data, game events, team statistics, player game statistics, player statistics, injuries, and standings for both the NFL and NCAA. Paid plans cover the same endpoints and competitions and differ only in daily request quota and seats.


- **Free plan** : 100 requests a day, with the quota resetting at 00:00 UTC
- **Pro** : 7,500 requests a day, one seat
- **Ultra** : 75,000 requests a day, two seats
- **Mega** : 150,000 requests a day, three seats


**Honest take:** The quota model is easy to plan around, and NCAA coverage on the same key helps if you build for college football too. A daily cap means you budget calls carefully on game days.


**Cons:** Unused requests are lost at the daily reset. Prices on the plan page exclude VAT, so check the total for your country.


Reference:[API-Sports NFL documentation](https://api-sports.io/documentation/nfl/v1) .


## 5. BALLDONTLIE


**[BALLDONTLIE's NFL API](https://nfl.balldontlie.io/) is a developer API with NFL data from 2002 to the current season and a free tier.**


BALLDONTLIE asks for a free account and an API key in the` Authorization` header. Its NFL docs list teams, players, games, stats, standings, player injuries, and player designations. The company also publishes OpenAPI specs and an MCP server, so AI assistants can read the API definition directly.


- **Free** : 5 requests a minute
- **ALL-STAR** : $9.99 a month, 60 requests a minute
- **GOAT** : $39.99 a month, 600 requests a minute
- **Trial** : 7 days of the GOAT tier for each league subscription


**Example:**


```text
curl   "https://api.balldontlie.io/nfl/v1/teams"   \
-H   "Authorization: YOUR_BALLDONTLIE_API_KEY"
```


**Honest take:** BALLDONTLIE is the cheapest way in this list to get two decades of NFL games and stats behind a REST API. The free tier works for prototypes, not for a bot polling scores every minute.


**Cons:** At 5 requests a minute, the free tier is slow for bulk backfills.


Reference:[balldontlie.io](https://www.balldontlie.io/) .


## 6. Highlightly


**[Highlightly's NFL API](https://highlightly.net/nfl-api/) returns live scores, game statistics, and player data along with video highlights for the NFL and NCAA FBS.**


Highlightly covers the NFL regular season, preseason, playoffs, and Super Bowl, plus all major NCAA FBS conferences and the College Football Playoff. Its highlights feed adds game recaps, post-game interviews, and highlighted plays, with a geo-restriction checker for each clip.


- **Basic** : Free, 100 requests a day, no credit card
- **Pro** : $7.99 a month, 7,500 requests a day, 12 requests a second
- **Ultra** : $18.99 a month, 25,000 requests a day
- **Mega** : $44.99 a month, 65,000 requests a day


**Honest take:** If your app shows scores next to video, Highlightly saves you a second integration. For deep stats like snap counts or odds, the commercial feeds go further.


**Cons:** Video availability depends on region, which is why the geo-restriction checker exists.


Reference:[Highlightly NFL API documentation](https://highlightly.net/nfl-api/documentation/) .


## 7. Goalserve


**[Goalserve](https://www.goalserve.com/en/sport-data-feeds/nfl-api/prices) sells NFL and NCAA data feeds at flat monthly or yearly prices in XML and JSON.**


Goalserve's NFL feed covers the NFL, NFL preseason, NCAA, bowl games, and the CFL. Its price page listed NFL and NCAA live data at $300 for one month, $1,500 for six months, and $1,200 for 12 months as a sale price. A US sports package and an all-sports package cost more.


- **Leagues** : NFL, NCAA, bowl games, and CFL in one feed
- **Formats** : XML and JSON
- **Trial** : Free trial period on request


**Honest take:** Flat pricing with no per-request meter is easy to budget for a site that polls often. The entry price is higher than the developer APIs above.


**Cons:** You request a trial through a form rather than signing up for a key.


Reference:[Goalserve NFL API prices](https://www.goalserve.com/en/sport-data-feeds/nfl-api/prices) .


## 8. nflverse


**[nflverse](https://github.com/nflverse) is a free, open-source project that publishes NFL play-by-play and player stats as data releases with R and Python loaders.**


nflverse ships as packages and data repositories rather than a hosted endpoint, and much of the NFL analytics community builds on it.` nflreadr` in R and` nflreadpy` in Python load precomputed data in one call, and` nflfastR` cleans play-by-play data and adds EPA and win probability models.


- ` nflreadpy` : Python port of nflreadr for lightweight data access
- ` nflreadr` : The main R loader for nflverse data
- ` nflfastR` : Play-by-play cleaning with EPA and WPA models
- ` nflverse-data` : The repository where the data releases live


**Install:**


```text
pip   install   nflreadpy
```


**Honest take:** For season-level modeling and research, nflverse is the standard free source. It isn't built for live scores or a request-per-question agent.


**Cons:** There's no live endpoint, so pair it with a real-time API if you need this week's games as they happen.


Repo:[github.com/nflverse](https://github.com/nflverse) .


## Why is an NFL API aggregator better than a single provider?


An NFL API aggregator puts several NFL data sources behind one API, so one integration covers data that no single source publishes alone. Firecrawl Alexandria works as that aggregator for NFL data, with NFL.com, ESPN, and fantasy sources such as CBS Sports and Draft Sharks on one Firecrawl key, each returning JSON from the same call.


- **More of the question answered.** NFL.com publishes the weekly practice and injury report, and ESPN carries box scores with passing, rushing, and receiving lines. An agent asked whether a player is active Sunday and how that player did last week needs both, and it reaches each through the same key.
- **One integration to maintain.** The APIs above authenticate differently (an` x-api-key` header for Sportradar, an` Authorization` header for BALLDONTLIE), return XML or JSON, and meter usage per day, per minute, or by flat price. Through Firecrawl Alexandria you keep one client, one response format, and one Firecrawl credit balance.
- **A fallback when a source lags.** On the sports benchmark above, ESPN answered 99.5% of calls at a P95 of 752 ms, and NFL.com answered 96.5% at 4.1 seconds. Both cover schedules, rosters, scores, and injuries, so an agent can switch to the other source when one is slow or erroring.
- **Room to grow.** Adding fantasy projections or rankings later means calling another provider on the same key, with no new vendor account or API key.


## Which NFL API should you pick for each use case?


Pick an NFL API by matching its freshest data and its price model to the product. Agents and chat assistants do best with Firecrawl Alexandria, because one Firecrawl API key reaches both NFL.com and ESPN, the data comes back as JSON an agent can read directly, and it works inside ChatGPT and Claude through the Firecrawl plugin. Sportsbooks and broadcasters need Sportradar or SportsDataIO. Hobby apps fit API-Sports, BALLDONTLIE, or Highlightly, and research fits nflverse.


Use case Pick Recommendation


AI agent answering injury, schedule, and standings questions Firecrawl Alexandria Can easily use with Firecrawl connected


Live betting models and in-play odds Sportradar, SportsDataIO Start with a trial, then contact sales for production pricing


Fantasy app with projections and DFS salaries SportsDataIO, Firecrawl Alexandria Firecrawl Alexandria: can easily use with Firecrawl connected. SportsDataIO: start with its free trial


Discord or Slack bot with scores API-Sports, BALLDONTLIE Start on the free tier, then move to a paid plan when you need more requests


Scores with video highlights Highlightly Start on the free Basic plan, 100 requests a day


Historical play-by-play research nflverse Free; load it with` nflreadpy` or` nflreadr`


## Building the top NFL APIs into your workflow


Most teams end up with one live source and one historical source. An agent that answers "who's out for the Chiefs on Sunday?" calls Firecrawl Alexandria for the NFL.com report and ESPN box scores, while a model trained on past seasons loads nflverse once and caches it.


If you build the product on a commercial feed, keep the agent layer separate. Firecrawl Alexandria handles the plain-English questions, and your Sportradar or SportsDataIO integration handles the live game screen.


To compare more top NFL APIs and sports sources before you commit, the[Firecrawl Alexandria sports page](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/categories/sports) lists every sports provider on one key, and the[fantasy page](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/fantasy) shows them working on real lineups. For the fantasy side, read[how Firecrawl Alexandria handles fantasy football](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/alexandria-fantasy-football) , and to set it up in ChatGPT or Codex, follow[the Alexandria plugin guide](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/alexandria-chatgpt-codex) .
